title: Burst Balloons
keyIdea: Pad with 1s. dp[l][r] = best coins from bursting every balloon strictly between l and r. Pick k as the LAST one burst in that range: then its neighbours are l and r, so dp[l][r] = max(dp[l][k] + dp[k][r] + v[l]·v[k]·v[r]). Fill short ranges first.

approaches.name: Interval DP (last balloon)
approaches.idea: I wrote this one (you didn't paste code). v = [1, nums..., 1]; for len = 2..n + 1, for l, r = l + len, for k in (l, r): dp[l][r] = max(..., dp[l][k] + dp[k][r] + v[l]·v[k]·v[r]).
approaches.why: O(n²) ranges, each trying O(n) choices of k.

quiz.q: Why choose the LAST balloon burst, not the first?
options: If k is last, its neighbours are fixed (l and r) and the two sides are independent

quiz.q: Why pad with 1 on both ends?
options: Bursting next to the edge multiplies by 1, and l and r always exist
Shorter intervals first, so dp[l][k] and dp[k][r] are ready
Left to right by l only
